Dependency elements may only be consumed by brokers.

What the Standard says

“Dependency” — A dependency represents an external capability the application relies upon but cannot control. Local code should only model such a dependency when it must inherit or implement that external contract, and brokers are the components that consume it. read it here.

Why it matters

Dependency types exist only to adapt objects imposed by an external package, so only brokers should consume them. Allowing them into services leaks third-party design constraints across the architecture and weakens the local contracts that protect the business.

Bad code example

// Violates STXD001: Dependency elements may only be consumed by brokers.
internal class StudentProcessingService(
    ExternalFrameworkDependency frameworkDependency)
    : IStudentProcessingService
{
}

Good code example

// Follows STXD001
internal class StudentBroker(
    ExternalFrameworkDependency frameworkDependency)
    : IStudentBroker
{
}
